title: The debt-close lint prints a start line and a line every 60 s while a Retire span runs, so a long close does not read as a hang
why: Finding (coordinator 13:46 CST Nov 14, from runner 10's logs ready3400.log and ready3400b.log; triage read none): `merge 3400 --ready` hung twice, 36 min and 11 min, after `ste-lint: PASS`. A python3 chain with a 600 s-old `sleep` child sat under it; no output, no timeout. Other PRs get the next line within 3 s. Debt candidate named by runner 10: the ready step has no timeout and prints nothing while a step waits, so a hang reads as slowness. Cost: 47 min of the runner's turn, n=1 PR, 2 runs. Cause on #3400 unknown; its lane is reproducing the single step now and was told not to run --ready. Not an owner question yet. Kin: merge-tool-beats-every-phase (a timed progress line per phase; its phase beat merged in #3404), stall-watch-ends-quiet-jobs, ready-checks-job-qualified-steps. First act of a lane: read what runs after `ste-lint` in `--ready`, reproduce the hang, then red then green: a `--ready` step that waits longer than its limit stops and names the step, and every step prints a line within a stated time. Check change: if a verdict moves, round 3 applies. REPRO 13:47 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 13:49): the #3400 lane cannot reproduce the hang on its head; runner 10 is asked for one more background rerun with a process snapshot at the stall. Cause still unknown. CAUSE NARROWED 13:57 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:00, runner 10's fifth run, process probe at a 65 s stall, its log ready3400e.log; triage read none): the stuck process is the debt-close lint, not the STE lint. The poller python3 (age 69 s) runs with cwd /tmp/debt-retire-<random>/tree; its parent runs in the claude-settings checkout and reads its pipes. #3405, #3412 and #3413 passed the same ready step, so it is PR-specific: one of #3400's six debt files (docs/debts/red-run-*.md and notes.md) may have a retire command that waits in a bare temp tree (unproven; the lane is testing it). Two defects whichever file it is: (1) the ready step has no timeout and prints no row while a debt command runs, so a stall reads as slowness (cost: 5 runs, about 90 min of runner 10 time, n=1 PR); (2) the lane's earlier guess (a step child holding ci-job's pipe, bin/ci-job:513-519) is ruled out for this case. Not an owner question. CAUSE FOUND 13:58 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:01; the #3400 lane reproduced it: its own `timeout 120 python3 lint/check_debt_retire.py --upstream origin/main --head HEAD` hit the timeout; `ps` showed a python3 with cwd /tmp/debt-retire-<random>/tree running hooks/test_guard.py plus 11 python3 children in test fixture folders; neither the coordinator nor triage read lint/check_debt_retire.py). Mechanism, from the lane's read of the file on main (judge_close, run_span): a debt closed by a PR has its Retire paragraph read from the base; each backticked tracked test file in it runs in a bare temp tree under TIMEOUT 1800 s. #3400 deletes two debts whose Retire lines name hooks/test_guard.py (full suite, about 39 min, measured once), so the ready step runs the whole suite and prints nothing for up to 30 min. SHARED DEFECT (tool, not edited; the tool fix is to be filed here): (1) no way to run one test family; (2) no heartbeat; (3) a debt whose Retire names hooks/test_guard.py cannot close in a PR without waiting out the cap; the same limit made an earlier check_debt_retire run read UNKNOWN at 1800 s. The #3400 lane fixes its own files (keep the closes with a Retire-run cite if the lint accepts one and a run of this tree exists, else restore the two debts). Cost: 5 runner runs, about 90 min of runner 10 time, n=1 PR. The earlier ready-step timeout idea stays as a second check: a step that waits past its limit says which one. First act of a lane: read lint/check_debt_retire.py, then red then green: a Retire line naming one test family runs only that family, and a long run prints a row at a stated interval. A lint that reads UNKNOWN at its cap is reported as unknown, never as clear. LANE STARTED 13:59 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:03; lane created 14:00 CST; tags cs-build:lane, cs-repo, cs-step:ready-step-hang-no-timeout; Sonnet, effort medium): brief is a heartbeat line in the debt-close lint at once; the one-family run and the close-in-a-PR design go to the coordinator as a `Departs from:` line before the lane builds that part; no verdict that turns a refusal into an ask or a pass. Owner stays the coordinator. PARKED NOTE 14:01 CST Nov 14 (coordinator 14:06, a pick of the coordinator's, undoable; neither the coordinator nor triage read the code): the lane found hooks/test_guard.py already runs one family via env GUARD_FAMILY=<name> (FAMILIES table; an unknown name fails the run), but lint/check_debt_retire.py cannot pass env today. The lane proposed `hooks/test_guard.py::<family>` as a runnable Retire span, a second accepted form where a prose refusal becomes a pass when that family passes. NOT BUILT: it widens what a shared lint accepts, moves a refusal to a pass on weaker evidence (a family that may not cover the debt), and would not help debts already on main (the lint reads Retire from the base). The lane builds only the heartbeat: a start line, then a line every 60 s while a Retire span runs; no verdict moves. The selector stays parked here. It becomes an owner question only if the owner wants faster debt closes, with the line "Goes against your ruling: a repo changes to fit a shared tool, never the tool to fit a repo", widens true, never recommended. Existing route for future closes: Retire lines name the covering case by function name plus a Retire-run cite. No owner item now. The title keeps only the heartbeat.
